question: In June 2025, the Bonn Climate Change Conference 2025 was held in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Germany**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bonn Climate Change Conference 2025** was held in **Bonn, Germany**, which has historically been a hub for United Nations climate-related activities.
 
• **Bonn** serves as the headquarters of the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**, making it a significant venue for hosting climate conferences.
 
• The conference aims to advance global climate negotiations, review progress on commitments made under the **Paris Agreement**, and strengthen international cooperation to combat climate change.
 
• Participants at the Bonn Climate Change Conference include representatives from **government bodies, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), scientists, and policymakers**, who discuss strategies for achieving sustainable development and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Bonn has hosted multiple climate conferences in the past, including the annual meetings of the **Subsidiary Bodies** to the UNFCCC, which focus on technical and implementation issues related to climate action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):**

 
 
• The **UNFCCC** was established in **1992** at the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, to address global climate change.
 
• Its primary objective is to stabilize greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere at a level that prevents dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.
 
• Key agreements under the UNFCCC include the **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** and the **Paris Agreement (2015)**.
 
• The UNFCCC Secretariat is based in **Bonn, Germany**, making the city a focal point for international climate negotiations.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• Adopted in **2015**, the Paris Agreement aims to limit global warming to well below **2°C**, preferably to **1.5°C**, above pre-industrial levels.
 
• Countries under the agreement are required to submit **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, outlining their plans to reduce emissions and adapt to climate change.
 
• The agreement emphasizes global cooperation, capacity-building, and financial support for developing countries to achieve their climate goals.
 
 
 
• **Bonn's Role in Climate Diplomacy:**
 
 
• Bonn is home to several UN organizations, including the Secretariat of the UNFCCC, making it a hub for international climate diplomacy.
 
• The city hosts regular meetings of the Subsidiary Bodies to the UNFCCC, which focus on implementing policies and technical measures related to climate change.
 
• Bonn also serves as a venue for preparatory meetings ahead of the annual **Conference of Parties (COP)**, where major climate decisions are made.
 
 
 
• **Important Conferences in Bonn:**
 
 
• The **Bonn Climate Change Conference** is part of the mid-year sessions of the UNFCCC, held annually to track progress on climate commitments and prepare for the COP.
 
• Previous Bonn conferences have played a crucial role in shaping global climate policies and advancing negotiations under the Paris Agreement.
 
• In **2017**, Bonn hosted the **23rd Conference of Parties (COP23)**, chaired by Fiji, which focused on implementation guidelines for the Paris Agreement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Germany's commitment to climate action:**

 
 
• Germany is a leading advocate for international climate action and has implemented ambitious policies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The country aims to achieve **climate neutrality by 2045**, ahead of the EU's target of 2050.
 
• Germany's **Energiewende (Energy Transition)** focuses on phasing out fossil fuels and increasing reliance on renewable energy sources like wind and solar power.
 
 
 
• **Subsidiary Bodies to the UNFCCC:**
 
 
• The Subsidiary Body for Scientific and Technological Advice (**SBSTA**) and the Subsidiary Body for Implementation (**SBI**) are key components of the UNFCCC process.
 
• SBSTA provides scientific and technical advice, while SBI focuses on implementing climate policies and reviewing progress.
 
• Both bodies meet in Bonn to advance technical discussions and prepare for the COP.
 
 
 
• **Global Climate Goals:**
 
 
• The **Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)** highlights the urgent need to limit global warming to **1.5°C** to prevent severe climate impacts.
 
• Achieving this goal requires rapid and deep reductions in greenhouse gas emissions across all sectors.
 
• International cooperation, technology transfer, and financial support are critical for achieving climate goals, especially in developing countries.
